questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking on the right or left, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Abruptly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: Before entering an expressway during your driving skills test, you must check traffic, use your turn signal, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually do not contain moisture, so they can't freeze.
Will remain slick after ice on other areas of the road has melted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will remain slick after ice on other areas of the road has melted.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer. Ice in these areas can remain slippery even after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: When making a turn, when should you cancel your turn signal?

options.text: In the middle of the turn

questions.explanation: Signal early and keep signaling throughout your turn or lane change. Turn off your signal once the turn or lane change is finished.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, you should watch the road about ____ ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead to spot obstacles and hazards early. At highway speeds, this equals about a quarter mile.

questions.question: If you need to drive down a hill, you should shift into a lower gear:

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. Shifting at high speeds can damage your transmission and prevent engine braking. Choose a safe speed that lets you control your vehicle without heavy braking. Consider the hill's steepness, length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: Failing to exit your vehicle properly during an exercise in the basic vehicle control skills test will result in:

options.text: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
An extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the test, face the vehicle and use three points of contact at all times. If driving a bus, hold the handrail. Improper exit may result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps keep an engine working properly:

options.text: While minimizing the vehicle's fuel use.

questions.explanation: Keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system at all times. Despite its name, antifreeze helps your engine run properly in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: If there are no warning gates or lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are likely abandoned.
Park your vehicle and walk up to the tracks to check for trains.
Look down the tracks in both directions to check for approaching trains.
Do whatever surrounding vehicles are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look down the tracks in both directions to check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look both directions down the tracks for any approaching trains.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead for hazards. Plan how you will handle them if they become dangerous.

questions.question: Your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not. What will the ABS do?

options.text: It will help you steer better.
It will let others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will help you steer better.
questions.explanation: ABS on the tractor will still help you steer better, even if the trailer does not have ABS. Watch the trailer and release the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of these will you NOT have to do?

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: You will walk around the vehicle, point to items, and explain what you are checking. You will not crawl under the vehicle or hood.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal hard for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal hard for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal hard for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times. Then press the pedal hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press it hard and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until you are ____ below your safe speed, then release the brakes.
questions.explanation: Brake until you reach a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brakes. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: Off-ramps:

options.text: Should not be used by trucks.
Should only be used if following another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Off-ramps have slopes and curves that can be dangerous for trucks. Posted speed limits may be safe for cars but too fast for large or heavy vehicles.

questions.question: Spring brakes activate when:

options.text: Tire tread is worn too much.

questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure falls to an unsafe level. When you see the low pressure warning, safely pull over and stop your vehicle.

questions.question: In an emergency, use controlled braking by:

options.text: Braking as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Braking with about half of your normal force.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements small while braking this way.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Wait for the air compressor to build 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving immediately after starting the engine.
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the air compressor to build 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems before you drive.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged because you cannot do anything about distant hazards.
Only encouraged when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This gives you time to spot hazards early and respond appropriately.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a motorist on the side of the road

questions.explanation: Accident scenes are hazardous because people involved may not watch traffic, and the scene distracts other drivers. Ice cream trucks create hazards by attracting children who may not pay attention to vehicles. People near stores are focused on shopping, not traffic.

questions.question: The most common type of foundation brake is:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, a driver can slow down by:

options.text: Letting the truck run out of gas

questions.explanation: If hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear to help slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: When driving, the steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
Held with both hands at the bottom of the wheel
Held with both hands at the top of the wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: Held with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands placed on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat
Apply the brakes about halfway while keeping the wheels rolling
Fully apply the brakes, lock the wheels, and hold the pedal down until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat
questions.explanation: The stab braking method involves fully applying the brakes until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels roll again, and repeat this process.

questions.question: Joggers wearing headsets:

options.text: Are usually aware of what is happening around them
May not be aware of what is happening around them
Can clearly hear sounds of traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic sounds and may not know you are there.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake
May make critical decisions too slowly
Is usually more careful than a typical driver

questions.correctAnswerText: May make critical decisions too slowly
questions.explanation: When tired, you will not see hazards or react as quickly as when you are fully awake. You will be slower at making important decisions.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work using mechanical force.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs on a vehicle that identify cargo hazards
A type of tire used in snowy conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs on a vehicle that identify cargo hazards
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the specific hazard class of the cargo.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: Operating a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal and results in loss of license for at least one year for a first offense. Any detectable alcohol below 0.04 percent results in being put out-of-service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start test, you should:

options.text: Not turn on the four-way flashers because this is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.explanation: When you stop during the stop/start test, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, pull off the road safely and check your tires.

questions.question: For a driver's side parallel parking test, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For parallel parking on the driver's side, drive past the space first. Then back into it, getting your rear as close to the back of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely within the space.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Only use turn signals if other vehicles are nearby.
Not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Signal even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a busy area near trees.
Park in an open area away from everything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in an open area away from everything.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Stay away from plants and other vehicles. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: What happens when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning light or wig wag will activate when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:
questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible. If weight is too high, the vehicle may tip over.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day. This removes oil and water buildup.

questions.question: Friction in a brake drum is caused by:

options.text: Brake shoes and linings pushing against each other.
Brake shoes and linings separating from the axle.
Brake shoes and linings pushing against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes and linings pushing against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction inside a brake drum occurs when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: In hot weather, check your tires regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure can increase with heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure can increase with heat.
questions.explanation: Hot weather causes air to expand. This can make tire pressure dangerously high. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as pressure will drop too low when tires cool down.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how weight is distributed.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight should be balanced evenly. Too much or too little weight on an axle can make the vehicle hard to control and can damage the axle.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Downshift before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control the vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for several brake uses if the compressor fails.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 brake uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several brake uses if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air so the brakes can be used many times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed trailer or open trailer must be:

options.text: Left loose so it can shift when turning.
Heavy enough that it will not move.

questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed or open trailers must be securely tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: While driving, your mirrors should be:

options.text: Used only when there is traffic.
Checked often, but only on cloudy days.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of what is around you at all times.

questions.question: When are most drivers least alert?
questions.explanation: Drivers are least alert at night because of tiredness. Alertness is especially low after midnight.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, you should NOT:

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely fastened.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter pins are in place.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter pins are in place.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is secure and firmly mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter pins. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks.
A noise made by air brakes.
A part that allows air to move freely in the brake unit.

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: Some air brake systems use alcohol to:

options.text: Prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
Make the compressor work more efficiently.
Lubricate parts of the braking system.
Prevent rust on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator that puts alcohol into the system to stop ice from forming.

questions.question: On a flatbed trailer, you must use at least ____ to secure cargo.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, no matter the size, must have at least two tie-downs.
